info.title: Divinci Public/Customer API
info.description: Public API for managing whitelabels, RAG knowledge bases, releases, fine-tuning, transcripts, and more. This spec is auto-generated from the Express route definitions in workspace/servers/public-api/src/api/v1. Every path here is served; a small number of served routes are not yet extracted (see docs/api/openapi-coverage.md for the exact count).

tags.name: chat
tags.description: `POST /api/v1/chat/completions` is an OpenAI-style completions endpoint for calling a Divinci release with the request shape OpenAI clients already send. Needs `transcript:write`.

tags.name: connectors
tags.description: Third-party source connections: list providers and connections, start a provider's auth flow, read and update its settings, disconnect, and run, poll or cancel syncs. Includes the web-crawl and WordPress starters. `connector:read` for reads, `connector:write` for changes. Stored provider secrets are never returned in plain text.

tags.name: divinci-agent
tags.description: Internal service-to-service endpoints for the Divinci Agent worker. Everything except `GET /health` requires the internal `x-internal-api-key` header, not a customer API key.

tags.name: export
tags.description: Whitelabel configuration as a file: `GET /api/v1/export` exports it (JSON or YAML, `whitelabel:read`); `POST /api/v1/export` imports one (`whitelabel:write`).

tags.name: html-pages
tags.description: Read-only access to crawled web pages: list, count, look up by URL or id, and per-host listings and crawl history. This group is read-only; pages are added by crawling (for example the web-crawl connector). Needs `rag:read`.

tags.name: mcp-config
tags.description: Internal: the MCP worker resolves a whitelabel's MCP settings here. Authenticated by the origin pre-shared key, not a customer API key.

tags.name: notifications
tags.description: In-app notifications: list them, read unread counts, and mark one read (`PATCH /api/v1/notifications/{notificationId}/read`). `notification:read` / `notification:write`.

tags.name: rag
tags.description:
Knowledge bases (RAG vectors): create and tune indexes (`/rag/targets`), upload and manage files (`/rag/files`), group indexes (`/rag/groups`), and retrieve.

**Retrieval only, no generated answer:** `POST /api/v1/rag/context` returns the same chunks chat would put in the model's context for a query — use it to feed your own LLM. `GET /api/v1/rag/search` is keyword (full-text) search across the workspace's indexes. Both need an API key with `rag:read`.

tags.name: tts
tags.description: Text-to-speech: `POST /api/v1/tts/generate` synthesizes audio (`whitelabel:write`); `GET`/`PATCH /api/v1/tts/settings` read and update the workspace's TTS settings.

tags.name: voiceprints
tags.description: `GET /api/v1/voiceprints` lists the workspace's voiceprints. Needs `rag:read`. Voiceprints are biometric data; scope keys that can read them accordingly.

post.summary: POST /api/v1/rag/context — Semantic vector similarity retrieval Body: { query, collectionId | groupId, topK? }

200.description: Retrieved context. TWO SHAPES: querying a `groupId` returns `groupId`/`groupName`/`vectors`; querying a `collectionId` returns `collectionId`/`collectionTitle`. The common fields are `chunks`, `sources`, `query`, `total` and `retrievalMs`.

content.description: Chunk text. Empty string when the source carried neither `text` nor `content`.

score.description: Raw similarity between the query and this chunk, as the vector index reported it (cosine or dot product, depending on the index). Comparable across chunks from one index; across a group only when its indexes share an embedding model. Null for keyword-only chunks and for a compressed (merged) chunk.

rankScore.description: The score retrieval ordered by when it differs from `score`: the manual-priority / recency blend, or a rank-fusion score. Not on a similarity scale; use it for ordering, not thresholds.

source.description: Filename or URL. Best-effort — prefer the response-level `sources`.

sources.description: Source filenames/URLs for the whole result. Authoritative provenance — per-chunk `source` is best-effort and often null.

total.description: Chunks returned after topK, not the corpus size.

vectors.description: Group queries only — the vectors searched.

404.description: No collection with that `collectionId`, or no group with that `groupId`, in the API key's workspace.

query.description: The question or text to retrieve context for. Surrounding whitespace is trimmed; must not be empty.

collectionId.description: ID of one RAG vector (collection) to search. Give this or `groupId`; when both are set, `groupId` is used.

groupId.description: ID of a RAG vector group, searched as one merged index. Give this or `collectionId`.

topK.description: Maximum chunks to return, capped at 50; zero or negative is ignored. Defaults to the collection's `contextPerMessage` (5 if unset), or the group's own limits. For a group it raises the per-index fetch and the merged cap to at least topK.

minimumSimilarity.description: Drop chunks whose similarity to the query is below this (0-1), for this request only. Defaults to each index's own `minimumSimilarity`. Lower it for indexes whose scores run low (dot-product backends such as Vertex AI often top out near 0.5-0.6). The value used is echoed back as `minimumSimilarity`.

200.description: The appended chunk's id and timing.

searchable.description: Always true — the chunk is searchable on return.

added.description: False when the backend deduplicated the chunk away.

502.description: The memory backend rejected or failed the write.

503.description: The workspace has no enabled mem0 resource. Configure one before appending or searching chunks.

results.description: Backend-shaped match records — passed through from the memory backend.

502.description: The memory backend rejected or failed the search.

503.description: The workspace has no enabled mem0 resource. Configure one before appending or searching chunks.

post.summary: POST /api/v1/releases — Create a new release draft
POST /api/v1/releases/:releaseId/publish — Publish a release draft

POST /api/v1/releases/:releaseId/deprecate — Take a PUBLISHED release out of service. The counterpart to /publish, which had no inverse on this surface: `DELETE /:releaseId` only removes DRAFTS, so an API-key client could publish a release and then had no way to withdraw it.  This is the withdrawal path for a rights refusal. WWW-RAG re-checks robots.txt before every crawl, but a host that ALLOWED AI use when we crawled it and refuses today was already published — and the only remedy is to stop serving it. Fifteen such sites were live on 2026-08-18 (Cloudflare's Managed robots.txt block names CloudflareBrowserRenderingCrawler, our exact crawler).  Deprecating rather than deleting is deliberate: the release stops serving (the public endpoint and the WWW-RAG directory both treat only `available` and `active` as live) while the record of what we published, and that we withdrew it, survives. A hard delete would destroy the evidence that the refusal was honoured.  ⚠️ Gated by `release:deprecate`, NOT `release:write`. Every other route on this surface acts on a DRAFT; this one retires a LIVE release, so a key that can publish must not be able to take a site down as a side effect. Pinned by scripts/ci/tests/test_release_auth_boundary.py.

POST /api/v1/releases/:releaseId/fork — Fork a (published) release into a new draft, carrying over its full config. Lets API-key clients (e.g. the local- inference extension's MCP tab) edit a live release's enabled tools: fork → PATCH the draft → publish. The handler enforces same-whitelabel ownership; the draft inherits skillConfig (catalogSkills/mcpSkills — see fork-as-draft model method).

patch.summary: PATCH /api/v1/releases/:releaseId/tools — Partial update of a draft release's enabled skills / MCP servers ONLY. Unlike PATCH /:releaseId (a full-object replace that wipes omitted fields), this touches just skillConfig.catalogSkills / skillConfig.mcpSkills — the toggle the local-inference extension's MCP tab needs.

PATCH /api/v1/releases/:releaseId/enrichment — Set the release's persona (threadPrefix), welcome message and conversation starters in one call, creating the three whitelabel-scoped resources on the way.  Like PATCH /:releaseId/tools this is a FOCUSED update, not the full-object replace PATCH /:releaseId performs — and unlike /tools it works on a PUBLISHED release, because the 4,687 releases that need it are published. See set-enrichment.ts for why that is the right posture here.  `release:write`, not `release:deprecate`: this changes how a release introduces itself, it cannot take a site out of service.

status.description: `orphaned` is computed at read time: the worker stopped heartbeating while the run was `running`.

get.summary: GET /api/v1/qa/runs/:runResultId One run with its report: per-release scores, answer and retrieval time (avg/median AnswerMs, RetrievalMs), the scoring-inclusive latency, and the per-test matrix. status "orphaned" means the worker stopped heartbeating.

200.description: One run with its comparison report. Timing per release: `medianAnswerMs` is retrieval plus generation (what a user waits for), `medianRetrievalMs` is the retrieval part of it, and `medianLatencyMs` adds every scorer's judge call (the QA run's own cost per test).

status.description: `orphaned` is computed at read time: the worker stopped heartbeating while the run was `running`.

perRelease.description: One row per variant (release, or release + RAG group).

passedCount.description: Tests scored by at least one scorer.

unscoredCount.description: Answered but scored by no scorer; never averaged in as 0.

avgAnswerMs.description: Mean time to produce an answer: retrieval + generation, no scoring.

medianAnswerMs.description: Median answer time. The latency a user of the release sees.

avgRetrievalMs.description: Mean retrieval time per answer (slowest vector; vectors are queried in parallel).

medianRetrievalMs.description: Median retrieval time. Part of the answer time, not added to it.

avgLatencyMs.description: Mean per-test time INCLUDING every scorer's judge call.

wallClockMs.description: The whole variant's run, concurrency included.

withFailure.description: Answers generated while a vector's backend had failed.

perTest.description: One row per test. Maps are keyed by variant: `releaseId`, or `releaseId:ragGroupId` in a RAG-group sweep.

report.description: Null until the run has produced a report.

orphanReason.description: Present when `status` is `orphaned`: why the run is considered dead.

get.summary: --------------------------------------------------------------------------- Admin lifecycle (API-key surface for the SDK / MCP / CLI)  Mounted under /api/v1/terms/admin — the `/admin` segment keeps these unambiguous next to the consumer routes below (a bare GET /:tosId would otherwise collide with paths like /accept). Scopes mirror the release admin routes: reads need `release:read`, writes need `release:write` (a ToS is release-governing configuration; no new scope to provision).  Attaching a ToS to a release is a RELEASE update — PATCH /api/v1/releases/:releaseId with { termsOfService: { id } } (drafts), or the release /update path for active releases. --------------------------------------------------------------------------- GET /api/v1/terms/admin — list the workspace's ToS documents

post.summary: POST /api/v1/terms/accept Records acceptance of the CURRENT published ToS version for the API-key-resolved user. Body: { tosId, version, releaseId? } — all come from the 403 TERMS_NOT_ACCEPTED `details`. When releaseId is supplied, the tosId must be the document that release references (same cross-check as the public accept endpoint). Responds 409 when version is stale.
